findings.title: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a new disconnected `TestLogger`, breaking test log assertions
findings.body: In `pkg/plugins/log/fake.go`, `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver `f`. In `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go` (line 58), `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. When a test passes a `*TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware(cfg, logger)` and later inspects `logger.InfoLogs` (such as in `logger_middleware_test.go`), all log calls are recorded on the throwaway `TestLogger` returned by `FromContext` rather than on `f`, leaving `f.InfoLogs.Calls` at 0 and causing existing tests and any caller inspecting `TestLogger` state to fail.

findings.title: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` dereferences `req` without nil checks
findings.body: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` immediately access `req.PluginContext` without checking whether `req == nil`. Other client middlewares in this package (for example `LoggerMiddleware` at lines 63, 77, 90, and 104) guard against `req == nil` and pass the call through to `m.next`. Because `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is registered ahead of `LoggerMiddleware` in `CreateMiddlewares`, a nil request that previously reached `LoggerMiddleware` (such as in unit tests for nil-request handling or callers passing nil) will now panic with a nil pointer dereference in `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`.
